sections.text: As soon as man understands that it is only the Qualities which act and nothing else, and perceives That which is beyond, he attains My divine nature.
When the soul transcends the Qualities, which are the real cause of physical existence, then, freed from birth and death, from old age and misery, he quaffs the nectar of immortality.
Arjuna asked: My Lord! By what signs can he who has transcended the Qualities be recognized? How does he act? How does he live beyond them?

So we had been discussing chapter 14, Gunatraya Vibhaga Yoga, Yoga of the three gunas. So far, in the first six chapters we learned about the conditioned consciousness -- I. In the next six chapters we learned about the Supreme Consciousness.
From conditioned consciousness to the supreme Consciousness is the journey which we all are taking. So to help that journey, in the last chapter we have defined what is the field and who is the knower and what is the differentiation between the two. So we have said that the I, the knower, know the field which is this body, mind and intellect.
I know my body, I know my mind, I know my intellect, therefore they are my field. And I, the knower, am the knower of the field. And the field cannot be the knower, and the knower cannot be the field.
Now, in this chapter we are learning about the qualities of the field. So we are taking it a step at a time to understand how I can take this journey from this conditioned consciousness which I consider I -- or in Vedanta called Jiva, the limited self -- to the supreme self which is my true nature. And therefore the quest in life is always to achieve that balance where there is no sorrows, no limitations, nothing that will create unhappiness, a perfect happiness.
And because there is no unhappiness, it cannot be called happiness, but just a bliss. So we have seen this and then we say these gunas. The Prakriti has three gunas.
The field which is part of the Prakriti has three gunas. These gunas bind the knower to the field. Those are the attractions which create bondage between the Purusha and Prakriti, the knower and the field, and create identification.
This identification is because of these gunas. And those three gunas we have seen as Sattva rajas and Tamas. My awareness about this field is Sattva; the activity, the passion for something I like, is Rajas; and then ignorance is Tamas.
These three bind me. So how do I get out of these three? Or is one of them helping me to get out of this conditioned consciousness to supreme consciousness? So we have seen that Sattva gives knowledge, Rajas gives activity. And the byproduct would be greed -- one activity leads to another and to another and another, and theres no end to it.
So that creates greed and Tamas creates inertia. So now we have to transcend from one to another. So one, the lowest we can see is inertia from our perspective.
These are the qualities of my mind right now. These are the qualities of the field. In this field the body is obviously completely inert.
By its very nature it just cannot do anything but to exist. Just like we have seen, the atom has inertia and therefore it exists. As long as the inertia is there, atom exists as an atom.
Once you disturb the inertia, the Rajas will explode into atomic energy. Body is nothing but inertia. But the mind and intellect have all three.
The Rajas, Tamas and Sattva. So these are the qualities of my mind which Im most interested in. And that depending on the quality of my mind, if it is Sattva, it has a knowledge.
Prakash, Gnaan -- if it is Rajas, Im active with new projects, new activity. And inertia -- dont want to know anything, dont want to do anything. So the verses you have seen now tell me what happens if one guna or another is predominant in my mental zone.
Urdhvam Gacchanti Sattvasthaha -- those who are established in Sattva. If my mental quality is predominantly Sattva, Urdhvam Gacchanti -- I go higher. Higher and lower are obviously concepts of my mind. Im going towards my goal -- going from the conditioned consciousness to supreme consciousness, to unconditioned consciousness.
This conditioning which is binding me, my goal is to get rid of it and become one with the unconditioned supreme consciousness. That which leads me to my goal, I consider higher. So Urdhvam Gacchanti Sattvasthaha -- the Sattvic mode of my mind will lead me towards my goal of unconditioning this conditioning.
Then, Madhye Tishthanti Rajasaha -- those whose mental zone is predominantly Rajasic. They remain in the middle. Neither are they going up nor are they going down.
They remain in a status quo. Just like in our election -- we ended up where we started. The Rajasic do a lot of activities.
But in the end if you see the sum total, the result is the same. If you can look at all the activities we have done in life. All we have done is to create security for ourselves, stability for ourselves, some kind of a protection that we remain in a good condition.
And in the end it all comes down to the same thing. Every few years we have to go through the same thing over and over and over again. So they basically remain in the same state they are in.
Neither are they making progress upward nor going downwards. Neither are they unburdening themselves from their bondages nor creating more bondage -- they are in the same state. Jaghanya gunavrittisthaha adho gacchanti tamasaha.
But those who are abiding in the lower qualities of Tamas, they go down. Obviously we are talking about human beings, about the human mind. The human mind which has evolved for activity and knowledge to understand the world around it.
The more it understands, the higher it goes. The more it gets entangled into this world, the more it remains where it is. The more it doesnt want to know, the more it goes down -- down in the sense of a situation where no more knowledge is necessary to survive, just the basic knowledge of I exist and I survive is good enough.
They go down into that state of existence. In the next verse we have seen: na anyam gunebhya kartaram yada drashta anupashyati. Why did we look at that verse? To introspect.
In the spiritual quest, introspection is the most important aspect of our practice. You have to constantly introspect and see what is there in your mental zone. And if I find any impurities, I need to remove them -- that is antahkarana shuddhi.
And then once I remove the impurity, the purity itself will reveal what is right and wrong. If I introspect and find myself to be in the tamasic zone, my next goal is to become Rajasic. Going from Tamasic to Sattvic is not an easy journey -- you have to go through Rajasic first.
Thats why the Bhagavad Gita says, the people who are doing good for the wrong reason -- let them do it, do not stop them. If Im giving a donation to make my name, Im at least better than the one who is not giving at all. Thats why the Bhagavad Gita says let them do it, for whatever the motivation.
But you need to make progress. So he said, if I am in a tamasic zone, let me make sure that at least Im active. If Im in an active zone, I need to slow down and understand why Im doing it.
That introspection leads me to what will be the remedy, to what my next efforts should be. And therefore the next verse says this is not enough. Generally we understand, well, if I go from tamasic to rajasic to sattvic, Im done -- because now Im remaining in the sattvic guna.
But we have also seen that even this sattvic guna is a bondage. We get used to doing good because people praise us: Well, you are really doing very well. So I want to keep getting that praise over and over again. In other words, you get attached to happiness.
The joy which comes out of knowledge, the joy which comes out of doing good, binds me to this. It does not let me leave. We have a saying in our architecture: what happens to the old architects? They dont die, they just wither away.
They continue working till they drop dead in the studio. Because that attachment to creativity -- that Im doing something, Im creating -- that attachment doesnt let you retire. So the bondage to Sattva is still a bondage.
The real goal for the conditioned self is to go beyond the gunas. And how do you go beyond gunas? Na anyam gunebhya kartaram -- there is no other doer in my life other than my own gunas. Only the gunas are the doers for everything which I am doing, accomplishing, and losing.
Yada drashta anupashyati -- one who starts seeing this, that all my actions are driven by the modes of my mind. Only when my mind wants to see Skyfall does it act on that desire. Meena says, read this chapter, its so nice.
But in my mind, Im going to see a Bond movie. Right now you can say whatever you want -- Im not in the mood right now. So who drives me to the Bond movie? Who brings me here to Gita class? My own gunas.
If I can recognize my mind as the doer and say, all that I do is driven by the quality of my mind as thought -- whatever my thought, my action will be driven by that. So all my actions I should assign clearly to my mind. All the gunas are doing what they do.
Na anyam -- there is no other. You can say, well, I was forced by society. Well, I really didnt want to go see a movie, but they insisted.
We used to do that when I was in college. I really didnt want to go just before the exam, but all my room partners said, Rajan, come on. I blame my room partners for why I went to see a movie just before the day of the examination.
But if I had no tendencies, I wouldnt have gone. So Bhagavan says Na anyam gunebhya kartaram -- there is none other than my gunas as the doers for all my actions. One who sees that -- Yada drashta anupashyati -- one who starts seeing that all my actions are driven by my mind and the qualities of my mind.
Gunebhyash cha param vetti -- and he says there is someone higher than these gunas, someone much higher than my mind, who also sees the limitations of my mind. Well, I shouldnt have gone to see a movie just before the exam. The I who says I shouldnt have is different from the I who went to see a movie. Gunebhyah param vetti -- one who knows that there is one who is above these gunas. Mad Bhavam sa adhigacchati -- identify with that.
I really dont need to take any credit or blame for my actions. My mind was in that mood and I did that. However, I am not my mind.
My mind is just a field in which my consciousness functions. That consciousness never took part in any of the action. If my identification takes place that way, Bhagavan says, Mad Bhavam sa adhigacchati -- he attains my being.
We have seen the supreme consciousness. Unconditioned by the limitations of body, mind and intellect, he becomes one with me. He doesnt become Krishna with flute and peacock feather.
He becomes one with that unconditioned consciousness. He now starts identifying with the room space analogy. Once the space leaves its identification with the walls, floor and ceiling -- remaining within the room -- it identifies now with the space outside.
Im none other than this universal space. Gunaan etan atitya trin dehi deha samudbhavan -- this dehi, one who considers this is me, this body, this mind is me, is created by these gunas. These gunas bound me to this body and said, this is me.

Verse 19 contains the pivotal teaching of this chapter: nānyam gunebhyah kartāram, there is NO doer other than the gunas. When you truly see this, everything shifts. That moment when you said something hurtful? Your gunas were acting. That burst of creative brilliance? Your gunas again. The one who SEES this, the drashta (witness), stands apart from all action. And Krishna promises: gunebhyash cha param vetti madbhāvam so adhigacchati, one who knows the Self as beyond the gunas attains My nature. This is not becoming Krishna with flute and peacock feather, but becoming one with unconditioned consciousness itself. Verse 20 reveals what transcendence brings: freedom from janma-mrityu-jarā-duhkhaih, birth, death, old age, and sorrow. The embodied self, once it transcends the three gunas that caused physical existence, amritam ashnute, tastes immortality. Arjuna then asks the practical questions we all ask (verse 21): How do I recognize such a person? How does he behave? How did he get there? Today, practice the essential shift: When you catch yourself saying I did this or I felt that, pause and reframe, The gunas did this; the gunas felt that. Notice how this creates space between you and your experience. The teaching uses a powerful example: The one who says I shouldnt have gone to the movie before the exam is different from the one who went. Who is that witness in you? Can you find and rest in that awareness today, even for a moment?
